aligned_segments.he: וזה מצה שהוא בחינת אור גדול מאד שממהרין לאפות מיד כי נצטייר האור מיד מלמעלה קודם שבא לידי חימוץ. כי חמץ הוא בחינת ציור ששם יש שני בחינות זכה נעשכה לו סם חיים לא זכה וכו'. כי חמץ הוא בחינת עץ הדעת טוב וע שיש בו שני כוחות כנ"ל כי חמץ הוא בחינת ציור שמתחיל התחמץ ולהצטייר כמו שאמרו רז"ל סימני חמץ כקרני חגבים אבל מצה הוא בחינת שאופין ומציירין האור הפשוט בבחינת ברכה קודם שמגיע לכלל חימוץ להצטייר למטה:
aligned_segments.en: And therefore throughout the year one may eat chamaitz — for one can also below depict the light for good and for blessing through the mitzvos of the Torah. And this is the aspect of the ten mitzvos that apply to bread — all in order to depict the shefa (flow of sustenance) for blessing. For eating is the aspect of shefa, the aspect of mochin, as is brought. And this is the aspect of mat'nos k'hunah (priestly gifts) — t'rumah and ma'asros. For one must give t'rumah to the Kohain in order to extract the grain from the curse with which the ground was cursed through the sin of Adam HaRishon — as it is written: "Cursed is the ground," etc. And therefore one must give t'rumah to the Kohain — for the Kohain can draw down the simple light that comes from Above, which is in the aspect of kamatz — closed and sealed — the aspect of "v'kamatz haKohain" (and the Kohain shall scoop) — and depict it for blessing. For the Kohanim are in the aspect of guarding the bris, through which their vessel is in a state of completeness — as it is written: "And Your covenant they shall guard." And as it is written: "A covenant of eternal priesthood." And this is the aspect of Bircas Kohanim being placed next to Sim Shalom. For the Kohanim, who are in the aspect of v'kamatz haKohain, draw down the light that comes from Above — which is kamatz and sealed — and depict it for blessing through Bircas Kohanim. And the essential thing is through the completeness of their vessel, since they are in the aspect of guarding the bris — for among the Kohanim there are more mitzvos regarding the holiness of the bris than among ordinary Yisrael, as it is written: "They shall be holy... a harlot, etc., they shall not take," etc. And therefore Bircas Kohanim is next to Sim Shalom, and the essential conclusion of their blessing is with shalom — as it is written: "And He shall place upon you peace." For shalom is the vessel that holds blessing — as our Sages said: the Holy One found no vessel to hold blessing for Yisrael but shalom. And therefore through this the Kohanim draw down the light that comes from Above — which is kamatz and sealed, the aspect of v'kamatz haKohain — and depict it for blessing through shalom, which is the aspect of the vessel in its completeness — for shalom is the aspect of guarding the bris, the aspect of: "Behold, I give him My covenant of peace." And therefore one prays regarding a dream at the time of Bircas Kohanim that it should be transformed from bad to good. For all dreams follow the mouth — for the dream shows a person that something is descending upon him, for good or, chas v'shalom, for the reverse. And therefore the essential dream is according to the thought in the mind — as it is written: "And the visions of your head upon your bed ascended." That is, according to the rectification of one's thought and mochin, which is one's vessel — so does the light descend upon one, for good, etc. And accordingly one is shown in the dream. And since the matter has not yet been drawn down below, but is only shown in a dream, therefore all dreams follow the mouth. For the essential completion of the vessel is through the mouth, where the mochin are revealed — the aspect of: "From His mouth come knowledge and understanding." And there is the essential completion of the vessel. And therefore through the mouth, which is the aspect of the vessel, one can depict the light as one wishes — for good or for the reverse. And therefore all dreams follow the mouth.
aligned_segments.he_nikud: וְזֶה מַצָּה, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת אוֹר גָּדוֹל מְאֹד שֶׁמְּמַהֲרִין לֶאֱפוֹת מִיַּד, כִּי נִצְטַיֵּר הָאוֹר מִיָּד מִלְּמַעְלָה קֹדֶם שֶׁבָּא לִידֵי חִמּוּץ, כִּי חָמֵץ הוּא בְּחִינַת צִיּוּר שֶׁשָּׁם יֵשׁ שְׁנֵי בְּחִינוֹת זָכָה נַעֲשֹׁה לוֹ סַם חַיִּים, לֹא זָכָה וְכוּ', כִּי חָמֵץ הוּא בְּחִינַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שְׁנֵי כֹּחוֹת כַּנַּ"ל, כִּי חָמֵץ הוּא בְּחִינַת צִיּוּר שֶׁמַּתְחִיל לְהִתְחַמֵּץ וּלְהִצְטַיֵּר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה, סִימָנֵי חָמֵץ כְּקַרְנֵי חֲגָבִים, אֲבָל מַצָּה הוּא בְּחִינַת שֶׁאוֹפִין וּמְצַיְּרִין הָאוֹר הַפָּשׁוּט, בִּבְחִינַת בְּרָכָה קֹדֶם שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לִכְלַל חִמּוּץ לְהִצְ

aligned_segments.he: ועל כן תמיד בכל השנה יכולין לאכול חמץ כי יכולין גם למטה לצייר האור לטובה ולברכה על ידי מצוות התורה וזה בחינת עשר מצות הנהוגות בפת הכל כדי לצייר השפע לברכה:כי האכילה בחינת שפע בחינת מוחין כמבוא וזה בחינת מתנות כהונה תרומה ומעשרות כי צריכין ליתן תרומה לכהן כדי להוציא הדגן מן הקללה שנתקללה האדמה על ידי חטא אדם הראשון כמו שכתוב ארורה האדמה וכו' ועלכ ן צריכין ליתן תרומה לכהן כי הכהן יכול להמשיך האור הפשוט הבא מלמעלה שהוא בחינת קמיץ וסתים בחינת וקמץ הכהן ולציירו לברכה כי הכהנים בבחינת שמירת הברית שעל ידי זה הכלי בשלימות כמו שכתו בוריתך ינצוור וכמו שכתוב ברית כהונת עולם וזה בחנית ברכת כהנים אצל שים שלום כי הכהנים שהם בבחינת וקמץ הכהן הם ממשיכין האור הבא מעלהמה שהוא קמץ וסתים ומציירין אותו לברכה על ידי ברכת כהנים והעיקר הוא על ידי הכלי שלהם שהוא בשלימות מחמת שהם בחינת שמירת הברית כ"ל כי אצל הכהנים יש מצוות בקדושת הברית יותר מישראל כמו שכתוב קדושם יהיו אשה זונה וכו' לא יקחו וכו'. ועל כן ברכת כהנים אצל שים שלום ועיקר ברכתם מסיימת בשלום כמו שכתוב וישם לך שלום כי שלום הוא כלי מחזיק ברכה כמו שאמרו רז"ל לא מצא הקדוש ברוך הוא כלי מחזיק בררה לישראל אלא השלום. ועל כן על ידדו ממשיכין הכהנים האור הבא מלמעלה שהוא קמיץ וסתים בחינת וקמץ הכהן. הם ממשיכין אותו האור ומציירין אותו לברכה על ידי השלום שהוא בחינת הכלי בשלימות כנ"ל. כי שלום הוא בחינת שמירת הברית בחינת הנני נתן לו את בריתי שלום:
aligned_segments.en: And therefore one prays regarding the dream at the time of Bircas Kohanim — for then the light is depicted for good. And therefore then one can transform the dream from bad to good — through the Kohanim who bless at that time, drawing the light from Above and depicting it for good and for blessing through the rectification of the vessel, through the aspect of shalom — the vessel that holds blessing. And this is what we mention in the prayer recited regarding a dream at the time of Bircas Kohanim — the transformation of the curse of Bil'am the wicked from curse to blessing. For this is the aspect of the tikkun of the dream: depicting the light for blessing, in the aspect of "Behold, to bless I have taken." And this is what we ask in Bircas HaMapil: "And let not my thoughts and bad dreams trouble me... and let my bed be complete (sh'laimah)," etc. A "complete bed" — this is the aspect of the tikkun of the bris, the aspect of the bed of Ya'akov, from which came forth the twelve tribes of Y-a-h, which are the aspect of a "complete bed," as Rashi explains. And the twelve tribes are the aspect of the tikkun of the bris (as explained in the discourse). And through this the vessel is in a state of completeness, and then the dreams are settled. And this is: "Let not my thoughts and bad dreams trouble me... and let my bed be complete." And this is the aspect of mat'nos k'hunah — t'rumos and ma'asros — in order to extract the grain from the curse, through the Kohain, who is the aspect of v'kamatz haKohain: he can draw down the simple light from Above, which is kamatz and sealed, and depict it for blessing. And this is the aspect of t'rumah to the Kohain and ma'asair to the Levi. For the Kohain is the aspect of v'kamatz haKohain — the simple light, kamatz and sealed. And the Levi is the aspect of tzairai, as is known — for Kohain, Levi, Yisrael are the aspect of Chochmah, Binah, Da'as. It follows that Levi is the aspect of Binah, which is the aspect of tzairai, as is brought. And therefore one gives t'rumah to the Kohain to elevate the grain to its root, which is simple light — the aspect of v'kamatz haKohain. And then it automatically leaves the curse, since it has been elevated to its root, which is simple light. And afterward one gives ma'asair to the Levi, who is the aspect of tzairai — so that the light and the shefa will be depicted for good and for blessing. And this is the aspect of challah to the Kohain, which is given afterward from the dough. For afterward, when the dough is made, the dough begins to be depicted and to leaven. Therefore one must give a second gift to the Kohain — namely challah, which is also t'rumah — in order to elevate the dough once again to its root, to the aspect of v'kamatz haKohain, so that the light will be depicted for blessing. For at the time that dough is made, the Sitra Achara can reawaken, chas v'shalom — for they are the aspect of chamaitz and s'or, whose hold is specifically at the time the dough is made, for that is when the essential depiction of the shefa that comes from Above occurs. For as long as the grain has not become dough, its process is not yet complete; the essential completion is when it becomes bread — from when the dough is kneaded. And therefore then is the essential awakening of the Sitra Achara, which awakens specifically at the time the light is being depicted, in order to depict it, chas v'shalom, in reverse. And therefore then chamaitz and s'or awaken — which are the aspect of depiction, the aspect of "the signs of chamaitz are like the antennae of grasshoppers" — which is the aspect of the depiction of the light, as is known to the understanding. And therefore we once again give priestly gifts — challah to the Kohain — in order to elevate everything to its root, to the aspect of v'kamatz haKohain, so that through this the light will be drawn from Above and depicted in the aspect of blessing. For the Kohanim can draw the simple light from Above and depict it for blessing — which is the aspect of Bircas Kohanim. And this is what is written regarding challah: "to rest a blessing upon your house." "To rest a blessing" specifically. And this is the aspect of brachah before and after — that we recite a brachah on everything — all in order to depict the light and the shefa, the vitality present in the thing from which one benefits, to depict it for blessing. And therefore one must recite a brachah before and after: before eating, in order that the light drawn from Above — the vitality of that item — should be depicted for blessing; and afterward, after eating, when the spirituality of the food spreads into the mochin and additional wisdom and da'as accrue through the eating. And each person receives vitality and mochin from eating according to his vessel — for in the case of the tzaddik, additional wisdom and da'as accrue through eating, and in the case of the wicked, the opposite — additional foolishness accrues through eating. Even though they both eat from the same dish — for it is all according to the vessel, for the vitality of the eating is drawn and depicted in each person according to his vessel, according to his capacity to grasp the mochin, for good or for the reverse, chas v'shalom. And therefore after eating, when the food begins to be clarified and the good and choice portion is drawn to the brain and depicted there in one's mind according to the rectification of one's vessel — therefore one must recite a brachah after the meal so that the light should be depicted for blessing at the time the vitality from the eating is drawn into the brain, which is the aspect of the vessel. And this is the aspect of Bircas HaMazon. And this is the aspect of HaTov V'HaMailiv that we say in Bircas HaMazon — saying three expressions of goodness — in order that the light should be depicted for good and for blessing. And behold, all of this applies throughout the year, when we are always engaged in depicting the light for blessing through the Torah and mitzvos. But now, at the time of the Exodus from Mitzrayim, before the receiving of the Torah — when they could not rectify their vessels in completeness on their own, due to the impurity of Mitzrayim — therefore we cannot eat chamaitz, which is the aspect of depiction: that we depict the light according to our own nature, according to the rectification of our own vessels. For the Mitzrim had seized hold of the vessels, and the light would have been depicted, chas v'shalom, in reverse. And therefore chamaitz is forbidden under bal yairah'eh and bal yimatzai — for then chamaitz is the aspect of a curse. And therefore we are compelled to eat matzah, which is the aspect of haste — for we do not wait until the light is depicted below. Rather, the light is drawn from Above in the aspect of blessing — the aspect of "Behold, to bless I have taken" — and this is the aspect of matzah that is baked immediately before it comes to leavening, which is the aspect of the depiction done below. For now we receive the light from Above in the aspect of blessing — and this is the aspect of matzah that is baked immediately. And this is the aspect of the four cups of wine. For wine has the numerical value of seventy — as our Sages said. For when one subdues the all-encompassing desire and merits to leave the exile of the seventy nations, which is the above desire — which is the aspect of the Exodus from Mitzrayim — then one merits the revelation of the Torah, which is the aspect of seventy faces of the Torah. And then one can drink wine, which has the numerical value of seventy, and merit through it the secrets of the Torah — the aspect of: "Wine enters, a secret emerges." And therefore wine has the same two forces as the Torah: "he merited — it becomes for him an elixir of life," etc. As our Sages said regarding wine: "he merited — he becomes a head; he did not merit — he becomes poor." For it is all according to the vessel, according to one's capacity to grasp the mochin. And one whose vessel is in a state of completeness through guarding the bris — he can drink wine, since he has already subdued the evil of the seventy nations. And therefore through the wine he can merit the revelation of the Torah, the aspect of seventy faces of the Torah — the aspect of "he merited — he becomes a head": the aspect of head and mochin, meaning he merits new mochin, the aspect of the revelation of the Torah. But "he did not merit — he becomes poor." And "there is no poor person but one lacking in da'as." For since he did not merit and his vessel is not in a state of completeness, additional foolishness accrues to him — for it becomes for him an elixir of death, chas v'shalom. For the essential rectification of wine is according to the rectification of the bris — as our Sages said: "One who sees a sotah in her disgrace should abstain from wine." That is, when there is a blemish of the bris, one must abstain from wine. For one can drink wine only when one has rectified the bris and merited to leave the exile of Mitzrayim — that is, from the evil desire of the seventy nations, which is the desire for immorality. And then one can drink wine — which has the numerical value of seventy — and merit through it the revelation of the Torah. And therefore on Pesach, at the time of the Exodus from Mitzrayim, it is a mitzvah to drink wine. And this is the aspect of the four cups, corresponding to the four expressions of redemption, corresponding to the four camps of the Sh'chinah — the aspect of the four banners, which are the twelve tribes of Y-a-h, corresponding to the twelve oxen upon which the Kingdom of holiness stands — "three facing north and three facing south," etc. — aligned just like the four banners that traveled in the four directions. And the essential tikkun of the bris is through the twelve tribes of Y-a-h — which is the aspect of Sh'ma and Baruch Shem (as explained in the discourse). And this is the aspect of the four cups of wine — in the aspect of the tikkun of the bris.

aligned_segments.en: And this is the aspect of eating maror. This alludes to what our Rebbe wrote in the above discourse: that the essential desire comes from the turbidity of the blood that comes from the spleen, which is the black bile. And therefore one must shed tears at the time of accepting the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven — in order to emerge from the above thoughts, for one who is habituated in them, chas v'shalom — see there. And this is the aspect of maror — a remembrance of "they embittered their lives" — the aspect of the above desire, which is the aspect of black bile. And therefore we eat the maror now — in order to sweeten and subdue and break the bitterness of the desire. For we dip the maror in charoses, which is the aspect of chas + Rus (as brought in the Kavanos). Chas + Rus — this is the aspect of the Kingdom of holiness, the woman of yiras Hashem. For Rus is the aspect of the woman of yiras Hashem, from whom Dovid descended — who is the aspect of the Kingdom of holiness. And chas has the numerical value of chayyim (life) — as is brought — the aspect of the woman of yiras Hashem about whom it is said: "See life with the woman whom you love." And this is the aspect of the tikkun of the bris — for the Kingdom of holiness, the aspect of the woman of yiras Hashem, is the aspect of the tikkun of the bris. And this is that we dip the maror in charoses — to subdue the aspect of black bile, the aspect of the above desire, through the aspect of the Kingdom of holiness. And this is the aspect of the seventh day of Pesach — the aspect of the splitting of Yam Suf. For the sea split into twelve parts — as it is written: "Who split Yam Suf into parts" — corresponding to the twelve tribes of Y-a-h. For the impure thoughts that come upon a person are the aspect of the depths of the sea (m'tzulos yam), as is brought. And the tikkun for the thoughts is Sh'ma and Baruch Shem, which have twelve words corresponding to the twelve tribes of Y-a-h. And therefore when the Mitzrim pursued them and overtook them camped by the sea — this is the aspect of the above desire, the exile of the seventy nations, the aspect of the exile of Mitzrayim, pursuing a person, especially at the time when one flees from it, when it intensifies all the more, as is known. And then the depths of the sea intensify upon a person — the aspect of impure thoughts. And all this is because they left before the appointed end, for they were not yet worthy of leaving. And therefore it pursues a person and seeks to overpower him — the aspect of the depths of the sea, which are the thoughts. And the tikkun for the thoughts, which are the aspect of the depths of the sea, is the aspect of the Sea of Sh'lomoh, the Kingdom of Heaven — the aspect of Sh'ma and Baruch Shem (as explained in the discourse). For the Sea of Sh'lomoh stands upon twelve oxen, which are the twelve tribes of Y-a-h. And this is the aspect of the splitting of Yam Suf, which split into twelve parts corresponding to the twelve tribes of Y-a-h, upon which the sea of holiness stands — the aspect of the Sea of Sh'lomoh. And then the raging waters — the depths of the sea — were driven out and nullified, and the children of Yisrael came into the sea of holiness on dry land. For the raging waters — the depths of the sea, the aspect of impure thoughts — that seek to overpower the sea of holiness, the sea of wisdom, for their essential hold is in a person's da'as (the sea of wisdom, for all thoughts and reflections are within the da'as and brain) — now they were driven out and nullified, and the sea of holiness remained standing upon the twelve tribes of Y-a-h. And this is the aspect of the splitting of Yam Suf into twelve parts. And the essential splitting of Yam Suf was through the aspect of Yosef, who is the aspect of guarding the bris — as it is written: "The sea saw and fled" — "and he went outside." For the essential aspect of the splitting of the sea is through guarding the bris — the aspect of the Sea of Sh'lomoh standing upon the twelve tribes of Y-a-h. And through the aspect of Yosef — guarding the bris, the aspect of "he fled outside" — through this: "the sea saw and fled." This is the aspect of: "From before Sarai my mistress I am fleeing" — brought there in the discourse. For the impure thoughts — the depths of the sea, the aspect of the evil kingdom — flee from before the aspect of Yosef, from before the twelve tribes of Y-a-h. And then the sea split — for the sea remained standing upon the twelve tribes of Y-a-h, and then the twelve tribes of Y-a-h could pass through it on dry land, walking and passing through the sea of wisdom without obstruction from the depths of the sea. And therefore at the time they crossed the sea, the sea of wisdom was revealed to them — as our Sages said: "A maidservant saw at the sea," etc. For the evil maidservant — the mother of the Airev Rav, the evil kingdom, the above desire — was subdued. And then even the lowest levels of Yisrael — even the maidservant of Yisrael — were all included in holiness, since the evil maidservant was nullified. And therefore "a maidservant saw" specifically "at the sea," etc. All this occurred on the sixth day of the S'firah. For even though on the night of Pesach a great illumination was drawn upon them, nevertheless afterward, after the first day, they went back to progressing from level to level through S'firas HaOmer (as explained in the Kavanos). That is, even though on the night of Pesach the light was drawn upon them from Above in the aspect of blessing, even though they had not yet rectified their vessels in completeness — nevertheless, afterward this illumination departed, and they had to receive the light gradually: according to the rectification of their vessels during the days of the S'firah, so they merited to receive the light of da'as — the holy Torah — on the fiftieth day, which is Chag HaShavuos. And this is the aspect of the 49 days of the S'firah, corresponding to the 49 letters in the acceptance of the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven in Sh'ma and Baruch Shem, which correspond to the 49 letters in the names of the twelve tribes of Y-a-h. And through the counting of these days, which are the aspect of vessels — for the days are the aspect of vessels and middos — through this one leaves impurity for purity and rectifies the days and the vessels, in order to merit receiving the light of the Torah on Shavuos in the aspect of blessing through the rectification of the vessels. And therefore on the sixth day of the S'firah, which is the aspect of Yosef — the aspect of guarding the bris — then the sea split into twelve parts corresponding to the twelve tribes of Y-a-h, which are the aspect of the tikkun of the bris. And therefore after the seven days of Pesach, chamaitz is once again permitted to be eaten. And as is brought in the Zohar — a parable of a prince — for after they received matzah, which is the remedy, they can eat chamaitz — see there. For initially they were compelled to eat only matzah, which is the aspect of the light drawn from Above in the aspect of blessing, not through our own agency — the aspect of "Behold, to bless I have taken." And through this they left Mitzrayim, from impurity to purity, and merited the aspect of the tikkun of the bris, and their vessels were rectified through this. And afterward, during the six days of the S'firah, their vessels were also somewhat rectified, and they merited the aspect of the splitting of Yam Suf into twelve parts — all of which is the aspect of the tikkun of the bris. And then their vessels were rectified, and they could depict the light in the aspect of blessing. And then they could eat chamaitz, which is the aspect of depiction — for then Yisrael could depict the light for blessing through the rectification of their vessels. And therefore on Shavuos we offer the two loaves of chamaitz specifically — for then we depict the light for blessing and receive the holy Torah in the aspect of blessing through the rectification of the vessels in the 49 days of the S'firah. And therefore we offer chamaitz specifically then — which is the aspect of depicting the light for blessing through the rectification of the vessels in the 49 days of the S'firah. Blessed is Hashem forever, Amain v'Amain. And therefore we eat matzah for seven days — for each day includes ten, and they correspond to the seventy cries corresponding to the exile of the seventy nations from which they merited to leave — which is the aspect of the Exodus from Mitzrayim. And throughout all these seven days one must eat matzah, which is the aspect of the light drawn from Above in the aspect of blessing — in order to subdue the exile of the seventy nations and to merit the aspect of seventy faces of the Torah. (And see well the entire discourse, "When evildoers draw near to me," from beginning to end, and then all these matters are explained properly.)
